title: fix(core): refuse a retired string `sort` ENTRY out loud instead of dropping it in silence
body:
Fixes #9955

## What was wrong

`packages/core/src/utils/sort-query.ts` refused the retired **scalar** `sort` clause out
loud, and dropped the **same clause one container deeper** in complete silence. The
author's row order disappeared and the console said nothing.

Re-measured at source on this branch's base, objectui `origin/main` `8a7e09fa1` — the
array arm had exactly two statements per entry, `continue` and `out.push`, and no sink
call anywhere between the `Array.isArray` guard and the return.

### Three arms, before and after

Each row is a real run of `convertSortToQueryParams` from
`packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/sort-query.test.ts` on this branch.

| input | `$orderby` BEFORE | diagnostics BEFORE | `$orderby` AFTER | diagnostics AFTER |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CONTROL A — scalar `'name asc'` | `undefined` | 1 (scalar message) | `undefined` | 1 (scalar message, byte-identical) |
| SUBJECT — `['name asc']` | `undefined` | **0** | `undefined` | **1 (entry message)** |
| CONTROL B — `[{ field: 'name', order: 'desc' }]` | `{ name: 'desc' }` | 0 | `{ name: 'desc' }` | 0 |
| CONTROL C — `[{ order: 'asc' }]` | `undefined` | 0 | `undefined` | **0 — unchanged, on purpose** |
| MIXED — `[{ field: 'a', order: 'asc' }, 'b desc']` | `{ a: 'asc' }` | 0 | `{ a: 'asc' }` | 1 (names `'b desc'`) |

Only the SUBJECT row moves, and it moves only in the diagnostics column.

⭐ CONTROL C is the load-bearing one. `[{ order: 'asc' }]` is also an entry that
contributes nothing, and its silence is **declared** in `normalizeSortEntries`' docblock:
"an entry with no usable `field` is SKIPPED (it names nothing to order by)". It stays
silent. That is what shows the seam was cut at `typeof entry === 'string'` and not at
"this entry has no field", which would have converted a designed silence into noise on
every partially-authored view.

## ⛔ The accepted input set is UNCHANGED — by one key and by one shape

`sort: ['name asc']` still contributes **no ordering**. Nothing that was refused is now
accepted, and nothing that was accepted is now refused. Making the array-of-strings
*work* would re-admit the retired spelling one container deeper and reverse the director
ruling quoted in this file's own docblock — decision batch #77, 2026-09-07, objectui#8221,
maintainer approved, option B: "The platform has one `sort` spelling, the array,
everywhere."

Loud is not accepted. Pinned, not merely asserted, by
`ACCEPTED INPUT SET UNCHANGED — the string entry contributes exactly nothing`, which
compares five arrays against their own string-free twins on both
`convertSortToQueryParams` and `normalizeSortEntries` — and which is the one new case
that stays **green under the ablation below**, because it pins the non-change rather than
the change.

The two docblock sentences that look contradictory are both still true, and neither was
edited:

- "Not a lenient alias: an unusable input (a number, an object, an array of strings)
  yields `undefined` rather than a guess" — governs the RETURN VALUE. Unchanged.
- "A retired string is REFUSED OUT LOUD, not dropped in silence" — governs the
  DIAGNOSTIC. This is the one that was being violated, and the only one this branch moves.

## The dedupe key — the decision, and why the line count stays bounded

**A sibling reporter, and ARM-TAGGED keys in the one existing Set.**

`retiredKey(ARM, SPELLING)` returns the arm token, a newline, then the spelling, so the
two key spaces are disjoint **by construction**: the arm token is one of two fixed words
and neither contains a newline, so the text before the first newline names the arm no
matter what an author wrote. A bare string prefix would only have been disjoint until
somebody authored the prefix — the spellings come out of authored JSON.

Why not reuse `reportRetiredSortSpelling` with the entry as its key:

1. **The sentence an author acts on differs.** The scalar refusal can say "this query
   carries no `$orderby`" because refusing the whole value refuses the whole ordering. One
   bad entry among good ones does not: `[{ field: 'a', order: 'asc' }, 'b desc']` still
   orders by `a`. Reusing the scalar text would tell an author their rows are unordered
   while they are ordered by everything except the key they are hunting for — worse than
   silence.
2. **On one shared raw key the first arm to fire silences the other**, so a page carrying
   both spellings would print a sentence about the wrong container. Pinned by
   `CONTROL A — the scalar arm is untouched, and the two messages differ`.

**The bound**: ONE line per distinct spelling per arm, however many blocks inherit the
same bad view. That is the property the existing dedupe was built for — this sink runs
inside the query memo of every object-bound block, so a related-list derivation over an
object with N lists re-enters it N times per pass. Pinned by `BOUNDED — N blocks
inheriting one bad view print ONE line, per spelling`, which drives 25 renders of one bad
view and asserts one line, then a second spelling and asserts two, then clears the seam
and asserts three.

## The message text

`console.error`, unconditional, not dev-gated — the same channel and the same severity
class as the scalar sibling, for the reason its docblock already argues: this REFUSES an
authored row order, so the page renders in an order the author did not ask for. Not the
`warnOnUnknownActionKeys` class, which reports keys nothing was ever going to read.
Asserted against `console.warn` in the same body.

Both halves objectui#9031 ruled load-bearing survive in this arm too, and they are judged
rather than eyeballed: the new case
`objectui#9031 — the ENTRY message prescribes metadata the installed spec ACCEPTS` parses
the entries back out of the **real emitted string** and feeds them to `SortItemSchema`
from the INSTALLED `@objectstack/spec`, exactly as the scalar pin does. The message names
`ARRAY_FORM_EXAMPLE`, states `order` is required at publish, and states that the ascending
default is a runtime tolerance and not permission to omit the key.

## One decision worth a reviewer's eye: the empty-string entry

`['']` stays **silent**, and that is symmetry with the scalar arm rather than an exception
to the seam. `sort: ''` never reaches the loud scalar arm either — the `!sort` guard
answers first, and the pre-existing case
`stays silent for values that were never the retired spelling` says why in words: an empty
spelling is "the author asked for nothing", and reporting it would train readers to ignore
the message. Inverting that one container deeper would recreate exactly the inconsistency
this card is about, in the other direction.

Whitespace is NOT in the carve-out: `'   '` is truthy, is loud on the scalar arm today,
and is loud as an entry too. Both legs are the control in
`the '' entry keeps the scalar arm's silence — symmetry, not an exception`.

## Reverse verification (ablation) — measured, on disk, from the committed state

Declared direction before running: turns RED. Run through
`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which proves the mutation reached the disk and proves the
restore:

```
anchor   x1 -> x0
replace  x0 -> x1
blob     ea88c7b574652c25132de1c60b8d457a346bf16b -> d046030a78eb15e235d3689f71bd65149bcac347
ok mutation landed
  -> Tests  7 failed | 32 passed (39)
ok restored: blob == HEAD (ea88c7b57465) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

The 7 that fall are exactly the new objectui#9955 cases that assert the diagnostic. The 32
that hold include every pre-existing scalar refusal — so the sink is demonstrably not dead,
and the new assertions are not vacuous.

## The plugin-grid pin this change invalidates — updated in the same branch

<sub>This section was rewritten by the `domain:ui#2` seat at 2026-09-19T02:04Z, under the standing clause that a dev writes a PR body once and the seat writes later corrections. It replaces a section headed 「⚠️ ONE RED」 that described a state which lasted one round; the evidence below is the seat's own and the implementer's, each attributed in place.</sub>

`packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/gridArrayArmOrderby-8973.test.tsx` had one case pinning
the very silence this card removes, and that pin **anticipated this card by name**. Its own
comment read:

> ⚠️ Deliberately NOT a new refusal diagnostic. objectui#8767 landed route C for the
> retired STRING clause; widening that refusal to cover the array-of-strings is that
> card's business, not this one's. This entry is dropped exactly as the shared sink drops
> an unusable entry — silently.

objectui#9955 is that card, and it landed the widening. The implementer stopped at the face
boundary and asked rather than riding; the seat granted route **A** (verdict
`5738396331`) and expanded the declared face by that one file, on three readings taken in
that act:

- open PR objectui#9924 modifies the same file — the module docblock, the imports,
  `afterEach`, and an appended section — and ⛔ does **not** touch this case's hunk;
- every `errorSpy` assertion on that branch is one of the three pre-existing ones, and its
  appended section carries **no** `errorSpy` assertion and no array-of-strings case at all;
- ⇒ the two edits are disjoint **in both directions**, so neither order breaks the other and
  the serialization the in-flight rule buys is buying nothing here — while the wait it costs
  is unbounded.

### What the update asserts

`expectNoOrderBy(params)` stays **first and unchanged** — the RETURN value moved nothing,
and that is the half a later reader is likeliest to get wrong. The diagnostic half becomes
`toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` plus three assertions that **discriminate** the entry refusal
from the scalar one: the message must carry the entry sentence's own opening, must **not**
carry the scalar sentence's, and must quote the value that arrived. A bare
`toHaveBeenCalled()`, or a match on `objectui#8221`, would be satisfied just as well by the
scalar message — and the input in this case is an **array**.

### The fence held

`git diff -U0` on that file yields exactly one hunk header, `@@ -188,5 +188,22 @@`. The
scalar-refusal case, the imports, the `afterEach` and the module docblock — PR objectui#9924's
hunks — are all outside it. `packages/core/src/utils/sort-query.ts`, its test and the
changeset are byte-identical to the first commit.

### The reading

Same command, same denominators, both sides: the composite affected set went from
`Test Files 1 failed | 165 passed (166)` / `Tests 1 failed | 3400 passed (3401)` to
`Test Files 166 passed (166)` / `Tests 3401 passed (3401)`. ⭐ The equality of the totals is
the reading — it says the one failure is gone **and nothing else moved**. The whole
`plugin-grid` suite is green on its own: 143 files, 1348 tests.

An advisory is posted on PR objectui#9924 (`5738398717`) so its author is not surprised; it
asks nothing of that seat.

## Verification

Run at commit `09d61f337`, from the repo root, per the repo's canonical invocation.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/` — **158 files, 3319 tests, all passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core run type-check` — **exit 0** (both legs: `tsc --noEmit`
  and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`), after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/core^...' build`,
  without which every reading is a stale-`dist` artefact (`TS6305`).
- Sink-aware consumers, run by name because the module's behaviour changed even though its
  exported symbols did not — `deriveRelatedLists.inheritSort`,
  `RecordDetailView.relatedListInheritedSort-5795`, `serverSorting`,
  `ObjectView.sortSink`, `ObjectView.namedViewSortArity`, `gridRetiredStringSort-8767`,
  `ObjectCalendar.sortMembersReachTheWire-8171`,
  `ObjectKanban.structuredMembersReachTheirSinks-8313`,
  `kanban-calendar-filter-sort-8174`, `ListView` — **all passed**.
- `pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` — the **whole repo**, not a
  narrowing: 5151 files linted, 95 errors and 13387 warnings, **every one of them
  pre-existing**; both files this branch touches report 0 errors and 0 warnings. The
  population and the file count are read from that JSON, not estimated.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` — OK, 8050 tracked text files scanned.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations` — 0 new citations, exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — 2 published source files changed,
  1 changeset declared, exit 0.

The one red is the out-of-face pin described above, and only that.

## Scope

⛔ Three things this branch deliberately does not touch, each declared out of scope by the
dispatch order:

1. The `field`-less OBJECT entry — its silence is declared in the docblock and is pinned
   as CONTROL C to keep it that way.
2. The empty array — objectui#9607, already closed as a measured no-op. Not folded in.
3. The `object-grid` wire shape — route B on objectui#8767, declined by the maintainer by
   name on 2026-09-10. Nowhere near this branch.

## Acceptance notes

- `noted, not filed` — the dedupe Set is now keyed by `ARM + newline + SPELLING` while the
  sibling sink `reportRetiredFieldType` (same module family, same "retired spelling" idea)
  still keys on a raw value. Not a defect and not filed: that sink has one arm, so it has
  nothing to collide with. Successor that would meet it: whoever gives that sink a second
  arm. Named here so the next reader of the two does not read the asymmetry as an
  oversight.

This PR is a **DRAFT** and stays one: landing is the claiming seat's act after review.
